08 / How it connects

Instructions travel. Custody doesn’t.

Trnzit sits between you and the providers you already use. It holds your instructions, policies and approvals. Your bank, exchange, custodian or wallet holds your assets and executes, exactly as it does today.

  1. Step 1

    You

    Members initiate; approvers approve, under your policies.

  2. Step 2

    Trnzit

    Instructions, policies and approvals in one place. No private keys, no custody, no funds.

  3. Step 3

    Secure API

    Your approved instruction is passed to the provider you chose, using access you granted.

  4. Custody stays here

    Your bank, exchange, custodian or wallet

    Your provider executes. Assets never leave its custody, and never pass through Trnzit.

How Trnzit connects, in four steps. One: you, or a member of your organisation, create an instruction such as a payment, trade or invoice settlement. Two: Trnzit checks it against your policies (approval thresholds, M-of-N approvals and whitelisted addresses) and collects the approvals required. Trnzit holds no private keys, no custody and no funds. Three: once approved, Trnzit passes the instruction over a secure API to the provider you selected, using access you granted. Four: your bank, exchange, custodian or wallet executes the instruction. Custody stays with your providers throughout. Balances and history flow back to Trnzit for display.

Governance

No single person moves your assets alone

For organisations, every material action can require more than one person. Set who can initiate, who can approve, and how many approvals each type of action needs.

  • M-of-N approvals by amount, connection or action type
  • Address whitelisting so funds can only go where you’ve agreed in advance
  • Separation of duties: initiators can’t approve their own requests
  • A full record of who requested, who approved and when
